newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG WINS SLALOM FOR OVERALL WORLD CUP LEAD.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG WINS SLALOM FOR OVERALL WORLD CUP LEAD.

text.p: Sweden's Pernilla Wiberg won a slalom for her second victory of the season to snatch the lead in the overall World Cup standings on Saturday as favourite Claudia Riegler could only manage ninth place.

The Austrian-born Riegler, who races for her mother's country New Zealand after disagreeing with her native ski federation, had won both previous slaloms this season, in Park City, Utah, and Crans Montana. She was third in the first leg but fell away in the second.
Wiberg stormed out of the starthouse on the Hirschenkogel piste and clocked fastest times in both runs for a winning total one minute 42.76 seconds and victory by more than a full second.
The Olympic and world champion overtook Germany's defending overall winner Katja Seizinger in the standings. Seizinger, who gave the weekend's races a miss, is now 68 points behind the Swede.

"It is too early to think about the overall. I will only start thinking about it after the world championships (in February)," said Wiberg, who has had her sights firmly set on the coveted title for the past few years.
Italian Olympic and world champion Deborah Compagnoni improved on a first leg sixth place to post an aggregate of 1:43.88 for second place.
Austria's Anita Wachter delighted home crowds at the small resort some 70 kms southwest of Vienna, by taking third place in 1:43.94, her best result of the season.
Another Austrian, Elfi Eder, winner of last winter's overall slalom title, recorded her best result of the season by finishing fourth in 1:44.50. Sweden's Ylva Nowen was fifth in 1:44.57.
